ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Based on the food web below, how many predators do the predatory insects have?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The food web diagram shows the node labeled "Predatory insects (lestids)" on the left-middle. From this node, one arrow points upward to "Large roach," and another arrow points diagonally/right toward "Steelhead." There is also an arrow pointing into the predatory insects from "Tuft-weaving chironomids." Reasoning: In this food web, arrows point from the organism being eaten to the predator. Therefore, arrows leaving predatory insects show organisms that eat them. The arrows leaving predatory insects go to Large roach and Steelhead, so predatory insects have 2 predators.
